title: File-based GNSS signal chain: gps-sdr-sim => GNSS-SDR => spoofing/jamming scorer
summary: A Docker (arm64/amd64) testbed that never transmits: gps-sdr-sim synthesizes GPS L1 C/A IQ for a static receiver from the shipped 2022-01-01 broadcast ephemeris, a numpy mixer adds noise, a second spoofer stream (power offset, time offset, ramp) and/or a jamming burst, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 processes each file into PVT, RINEX and a PVT dump, and an adapter feeds 1 Hz epochs (position, Doppler velocity, HDOP, clock, per-SV C/N0, plus no-fix epochs when PVT stops) into the gnss-interference-monitor scorer, with and without a static velocity reference, and reports time-to-detect, silent windows and false alarms. Four scenarios: clean, unaligned overpower, jam-then-spoof, and a code/carrier-aligned drag-off that walks the fix 978 m away.
verified: Ran end to end twice on 2026-11-06 with Docker arm64 on Apple Silicon (second run: image rebuilt, ./run.sh 319 s): gps-sdr-sim commit 28ca29a, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 package), RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 rnx2rtkp. Real outputs of the second run are in out/ and quoted in the README. Clean: median horizontal error 2.9 m, 0 alarm epochs in both reference modes. Drag-off: PVT captured to 977.8 m off truth; the old scorer alerted at t=138 (run 1: t=67 with a 43 s silent stretch), the new scorer at t=89 (constant-velocity prior) / t=86 (static reference), 9 / 6 s after the drag began, with no silent epoch after the first alert. Unaligned overpower and jam-then-spoof caused a GNSS-SDR PVT outage, not a capture; the old scorer gave 1 and 0 alert epochs, the new one latched a lost-fix alarm at t=81 and t=76 and held it to the end. GNSS-SDR runs are not bit-identical. Not validated against a hardware receiver; the AGC input is a file-power proxy; the static velocity reference is ideal.
